mainTopic: Who may write a גט and whether the writing or the signing must be לשמה (רבי מאיר vs. רבי אלעזר), and who may serve as a שליח to bring a גט.
overview: The amud opens with רב הונא's rule that a חרש, שוטה or קטן may write a גט only if a גדול supervises. רב נחמן challenges this from a גוי, then retracts. He explains that the ברייתא disqualifying a גוי follows רבי אלעזר, who requires the writing itself to be לשמה. רב נחמן then reports that for רבי מאיר, even a גט found in the garbage is כשר if it is signed for the woman, because the signing is what must be לשמה. רבא challenges this three times, and each challenge is answered. Next, שמואל and עולא explain the earlier משנה according to רבי אלעזר: the writer must leave the תורף blank. There are two conflicting reports of רבי יוחנן's view, which turn out to be a disagreement between אמוראים. A new משנה lists who may not bring a גט and teaches that the שליח must have דעת at the beginning and the end. The גמרא then debates why a סומא is excluded, and רב יוסף's answer about 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם' is upheld. The amud ends as רבי אמי begins to answer whether an עבד can receive a גט for a woman; his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A קטן may write a גט only with a גדול supervising
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא limits the משנה: a חרש, שוטה or קטן may write a גט only when a גדול stands over him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that is only when an adult was standing over him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא adds a condition to the משנה. People who are not legally mature may write a גט only if a grown-up supervises them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט must be written לשמה, for the sake of this particular woman. A חרש, שוטה or קטן cannot have that intention on his own. So a גדול has to stand over him and direct the writing for her sake.

keyTerms.meaning: And that is only when (adds a condition)
An adult, a legally mature person
Standing over him, supervising him

phrases.english: And that is when an adult was
phrases.notes: This is רב הונא, explaining the משנה's rule that even a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person or a minor may write a גט.

phrases.english: standing over him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהוּא שֶׁהָיָה גָּדוֹל עוֹמֵד עַל גַּבָּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the משנה's statement that all are fit to write a גט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חרש, שוטה or קטן may write a גט only under the supervision of a גדול.

steps.title: Then a gentile with a Jewish supervisor should be valid too
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן argues that by רב הונא's logic a supervised גוי should be כשר to write a גט, yet a ברייתא says a גוי is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: If so, then a gentile with a Jew standing over him should also be valid! And if you say yes, he is valid, isn't it taught in a ברייתא that a gentile is disqualified?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks רב הונא's rule by applying it to a גוי. A ברייתא says a גוי may not write a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If supervision is enough to make an unqualified writer acceptable, it should work for a גוי as well. But the ברייתא says a גוי is פסול. So it seems supervision does not fix the problem, and רב הונא's rule is in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, according to your logic (opens a challenge)
So too, likewise
And if you would say
Valid, fit

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said to him:
But if that is so, a gentile
with a Jew standing over him,
is he also valid?!
And if you would say, yes, he is,
but isn't it taught: A gentile is disqualified!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that supervision by a גדול makes the writing valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Extending the logic to a supervised גוי leads to a result the ברייתא rejects, since it says a גוי is פסול.

steps.title: A gentile acts on his own mind
steps.stepSummary: A גוי is different, because he writes based on his own intentions and does not just follow the supervisor.
steps.simpleTranslation: A gentile acts according to his own mind.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers רב נחמן. A גוי cannot be compared to a קטן or a שוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קטן or a שוטה has no real intention of his own, so he simply follows the supervisor's instructions. A גוי is a thinking adult with his own intentions. So we cannot rely on the supervisor's intent being carried out through him.

keyTerms.meaning: A gentile, a non-Jew
According to his own mind or intention
Acts, does

phrases.english: A gentile acts according to his own mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A supervised גוי is the same as a supervised קטן.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גוי has his own intentions, so supervision does not help. A קטן follows the supervisor, so supervision does help.

steps.title: רב נחמן retracts: a gentile may in fact write a גט
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן takes back his challenge. The משנה excludes a גוי only from bringing a גט, which shows he is כשר for writing one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן then said: What I said is not correct. Since the משנה disqualifies a gentile for bringing a גט, we can infer that for writing he is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן withdraws his own challenge. He brings an inference from the משנה showing that a גוי is actually allowed to write a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Later on, the משנה lists a גוי among those who are פסול to bring a גט. It does not list him among those who are פסול to write one. This silence shows a גוי is כשר for כתיבה, so the challenge built on 'a גוי is פסול' falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Then went back, changed his mind
It is not a correct statement
Bringing (delivering the גט as an agent)
By implication, one can infer
Writing

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the default view of the משנה is that a גוי may write a גט. That forces the גמרא to explain the ברייתא that disagrees.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman then said:
What I said is not correct;
for since it disqualifies a gentile
with regard to bringing,
phrases.notes: He means the next משנה, which lists a גוי among those who may not deliver a גט.

phrases.english: we infer that with regard to writing he is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: לָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא דַּאֲמַרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב נחמן withdraws the premise of his own challenge from step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב נחמן's own challenge, which assumed a גוי is פסול to write a גט.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה implies a גוי is כשר for writing, since it excludes him only from bringing.

steps.title: But a ברייתא says a gentile is disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: how can a גוי be כשר to write, when the ברייתא says a גוי is פסול?
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught: A gentile is disqualified!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן's new position with the same ברייתא from before. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the ברייתא is not used against רב הונא. It is used against the inference that a גוי is כשר to write. The משנה and the ברייתא seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Disqualified, invalid
A teaching of the תנאים not included in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: The words here are the same as at the end of step 2, but the job is different. There they challenged רב הונא; here they challenge רב נחמן's inference that a גוי may write.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: A gentile is disqualified!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that a גוי is כשר to write a גט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An explicit ברייתא states that a גוי is פסול.

steps.title: The baraita follows רבי אלעזר, who requires the writing to be for her sake
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר. He holds that עדי מסירה make the divorce happen, so the writing must be לשמה, and a גוי cannot be trusted for that.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר, who says the witnesses of delivery effect the divorce, so we need the writing to be for her sake. A gentile certainly acts on his own mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the ברייתא by saying it follows רבי אלעזר's view. The משנה, which allows a גוי to write, follows a different view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אלעזר, the witnesses who see the handing over make the divorce work, not the signing witnesses. So the requirement of לשמה falls on the writing itself. A גוי acts on his own mind, so his writing cannot count as לשמה, even with supervision.

keyTerms.meaning: That teaching follows the view of...
Witnesses who see the גט handed to the woman
They effect the separation (make the divorce work)
For her sake, for this specific woman
Certainly

steps.whatToRemember: Whether a גוי may write a גט depends on the מחלוקת about who makes the divorce work. For רבי אלעזר, the writing must be לשמה, so a גוי is פסול. The משנה, which only excludes him from bringing, holds he may write.

phrases.english: That follows Rabbi Elazar, who said:
The witnesses of delivery effect the divorce,
and we require writing for her sake;
phrases.notes: The requirement comes from the words 'וכתב לה' (דברים 24:1). For רבי אלעזר, it applies to the writing itself, not the signing.

phrases.english: and certainly a gentile
acts according to his own mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא states the accepted law, which contradicts the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר, who requires the writing itself to be לשמה. The משנה follows the view that allows a גוי to write.

steps.title: A גט found in the garbage can be valid according to רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן reports that רבי מאיר would say that even a גט found in a garbage heap is כשר, as long as it is signed and then given to the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: רבי מאיר would say that even if the husband found the גט in a garbage heap, had it signed, and gave it to her, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן tells us a surprising ruling of רבי מאיר. A גט that was not written for this woman at all can still work, as long as the witnesses sign it for her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that the witnesses' signature is what makes the divorce happen. So only the signing has to be done לשמה, for this specific woman. Who wrote the text, or why it was written, does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: A garbage heap
He had it signed by witnesses
Valid

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a general rule that a found גט works. It only works because the signing is done לשמה, according to רבי מאיר's view.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
Rabbi Meir would say:
Even if he found it in a garbage heap,
phrases.notes: He means a גט that happens to have the same names as this husband and wife.

phrases.english: had it signed, and gave it to her – it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, אוֹמֵר הָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about רבי מאיר's view of לשמה, as a contrast to רבי אלעזר's view in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, only the signing must be לשמה. A גט found in the garbage, then signed and given for this woman, is כשר.

steps.title: The פסוק 'and he writes her' seems to require the writing to be for her
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן from the פסוק 'וכתב לה', which teaches לשמה and seems to be talking about the writing of the גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged רב נחמן: 'And he writes her' means it must be for her sake. Isn't that talking about writing the גט?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's statement. The פסוק talks about 'writing,' so the writing itself should have to be לשמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the writing must be לשמה, a גט found in the garbage was not written for this woman and should be פסול. That goes against רב נחמן's report of רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he writes her,' from the פסוק about divorce
For her sake, meaning for this specific woman
The writing of the גט

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection to Rav Naḥman:
"And he writes her" – for her sake;
What, is it not the writing of the get?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that, for רבי מאיר, only the signing must be לשמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says 'writes,' so the writing itself should have to be לשמה, and a found גט would then be פסול.

steps.title: The פסוק is about the witnesses' signing
steps.stepSummary: The answer: 'וכתב לה' refers to the signing of the witnesses, not to the writing of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means the signing of the witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב נחמן. It reads the 'writing' in the פסוק as the witnesses' signatures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A signature is also a kind of writing. So for רבי מאיר, the פסוק's demand for לשמה is fulfilled when the witnesses sign for her.

keyTerms.meaning: The signing of the witnesses

phrases.english: No, the signing of the witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Writes' means writing the text of the גט.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Writes' means the witnesses' signing, which is what must be לשמה.

steps.title: A משנה says a גט not written for a woman is invalid
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges again from a משנה: any גט written not for a specific woman is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged him: Any גט that was written not for the sake of a woman is invalid!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a second challenge. A משנה clearly says 'written,' which seems to mean the writing must be לשמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This source is harder to explain away than the פסוק, because the משנה says plainly that a גט 'written' not for her is פסול. A found גט fits exactly that description.

keyTerms.meaning: That was written
Not for the sake of a specific woman
Invalid

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection to him:
Any get that was written
not for the sake of a woman – is invalid!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רָבָא: כׇּל גֵּט שֶׁנִּכְתַּב שֶׁלֹּא לְשׁוּם אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge against step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's version of רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says a גט 'written' not for her is פסול, which points to the writing needing לשמה.

steps.title: Read the משנה as 'signed'
steps.stepSummary: The answer: according to רבי מאיר, read the משנה as 'a גט that was signed not for a woman is פסול.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: one that was signed not for the sake of a woman is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing the word in the משנה from 'written' to 'signed.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same idea as step 9. For רבי מאיר, the place where לשמה matters is the signing, so the משנה is read to match that view.

keyTerms.meaning: Say, read it as: a way of changing how we read a source
That was signed

phrases.english: Say: that was signed
not for the sake of a woman – is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה requires the writing to be לשמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי מאיר, the משנה is read as requiring the signing to be לשמה.

steps.title: Writing the key part for her counts as writing the standard part for her
steps.stepSummary: רבא's third challenge: a source says that when the תורף is written for her, it is as if the טופס was written for her. This implies the writing must be לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: When he writes it, it is as if he writes it for her sake. Doesn't this mean that when he writes the key part for her sake, it is as if he wrote the standard part for her sake?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a third challenge. A source talks about writing parts of the גט for her, so the writing must matter for לשמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only the signing mattered, there would be no reason to discuss writing the תורף or the טופס לשמה. The source assumes the writing needs לשמה, which goes against רב נחמן. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: The key, personal part of the גט, with the names and date
The standard text that is the same in every גט
As if

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two parts. The תורף is the personal part with the names, and the טופס is the general wording that is the same in every גט.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him: When he writes it –
it is as though he writes it for her sake.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי, לָאו כְּשֶׁהוּא כּוֹתְבוֹ לַתּוֹרֶף לִשְׁמָהּ –
phrases.english: What, is it not that when he writes the essential part for her sake –
it is as though he writes the standard part for her sake?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: כְּשֶׁהוּא כּוֹתְבוֹ כְּאִילּוּ כּוֹתְבוֹ לִשְׁמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge against step 7, after the first two were answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that, for רבי מאיר, the writing does not need לשמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source talks about writing the תורף לשמה, which shows that the writing itself needs לשמה.

steps.title: Signing for her counts as writing for her
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers רבא's third challenge: according to רבי מאיר, the source means that when the witnesses sign for her, it counts as if the גט were written for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. When he signs it for her sake, it is as if he wrote it for her sake.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן pushes back on רבא's third challenge. He reads the source as talking about signing, not writing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's source seemed to say the writing itself must be לשמה. רב נחמן gives the same kind of answer as before: according to רבי מאיר, what matters is the signing. When the signing is לשמה, it counts as though the whole גט was written לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: He signs it (the witnesses' signing of the גט)
As if, as though
For her sake, done specifically for this woman

phrases.english: No; when he signs it for her sake
phrases.notes: This is רב נחמן answering, explaining the source the way רבי מאיר would.

phrases.english: it is as if he wrote it for her sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12 by reading 'writing' as 'signing.'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the source (writing means signing)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The source requires the text of the גט to be written לשמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי מאיר, only the signing must be לשמה, and signing לשמה is treated as if the whole גט were written לשמה.

steps.title: Another answer: these sources follow רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: A second answer to all of רבא's challenges: those sources follow רבי אלעזר, who holds that the witnesses to the handing-over make the divorce work.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: whose opinion are these teachings? They follow רבי אלעזר, who said that the witnesses to the handing-over make the divorce work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different way to answer רבא. It does not reread his sources; it says they simply follow a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר, the signatures are not what make the divorce work, so the writing itself must be לשמה. רבא's sources match רבי אלעזר. That does not disprove רב נחמן, who was only reporting what רבי מאיר would hold.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces a second answer)
Whose (opinion) is it?
Witnesses who watch the גט being handed to the woman
They 'cut' — they are what makes the divorce take effect

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
These teachings, whose opinion are they?
phrases.notes: He means the sources רבא quoted against רב נחמן.

phrases.english: It is רבי אלעזר,
who said: the witnesses of the handing-over make the divorce work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, broader answer covering all of רבא's challenges.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the sources to a different תנא (רבי אלעזר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's sources prove that the writing must be לשמה, against רב נחמן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Those sources follow רבי אלעזר; רב נחמן was stating רבי מאיר's view, so there is no contradiction.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: the signing witnesses make the divorce work (עדי חתימה כרתי). רבי אלעזר: the handing-over witnesses make it work (עדי מסירה כרתי). This difference decides whether the writing itself must be לשמה.

steps.title: שמואל and עולא: only if the essential section was left blank
steps.stepSummary: שמואל, and also עולא, say that the משנה's case works only if the writer left room for the תורף. עולא adds that the משנה follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: this applies only when he left the place of the essential section blank. And רבי חגא said the same in the name of עולא: only when he left the place of the essential section blank, and the משנה follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: Now a new explanation of the משנה begins. שמואל, and עולא as well, limit the משנה's case to a גט where the essential section was left blank.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The writer who is not qualified may write only the general text. The תורף, the part that names this woman, is filled in later by someone qualified, and that part is written לשמה. This fits רבי אלעזר, who needs the writing to be לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: He left over, left blank
The spot for the essential section of the גט (names, date and so on)
And similarly, and so too
In the name of

phrases.english: And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל:
And that is only when he left the place of the essential section blank.
phrases.notes: 'That' points back to the משנה letting even someone not normally qualified write a גט.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי חַגָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא:
phrases.english: And so too רבי חגא said in the name of עולא:
And that is only when he left the place of the essential section blank,
and it follows רבי אלעזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: וְהוּא שֶׁשִּׁיֵּיר מְקוֹם הַתּוֹרֶף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the challenge-and-answer exchange and gives a different explanation of the משנה, based on רבי אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unqualified person may write the גט only if the תורף is left blank, to be written לשמה later. This follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two parts of the גט: the תורף is the personal, essential section, and the טופס is the general standard text. Only the תורף is being saved for the qualified writer.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: 'It is not Torah'
steps.stepSummary: רבי זריקא reports a short, puzzling statement from רבי יוחנן: 'It is not Torah.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי זריקא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: it is not Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא gives a different view of the משנה. His wording is unclear, which sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the words 'it is not Torah' are left unexplained. The גמרא will explain them right away.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not Torah (meaning explained in the next steps)

phrases.english: And רבי זריקא said in the name of רבי יוחנן:
It is not Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי זְרִיקָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵינָהּ תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing view to שמואל and עולא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: 'It is not Torah' (still to be explained).

steps.title: What does 'it is not Torah' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יוחנן meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'it is not Torah' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of רבי יוחנן's unclear words. This sets up רבי אבא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack. It is a simple request to explain what רבי יוחנן meant.

keyTerms.meaning: What? (asks for an explanation)

phrases.english: What does 'it is not Torah' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of רבי יוחנן's phrase 'it is not Torah.'

steps.title: רבי אבא: writing לשמה has no force; this follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא explains: רבי יוחנן is teaching that there is no force to requiring the writing to be לשמה, following רבי מאיר, who holds that the signing witnesses make the divorce work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: here he lets you know that 'for her sake' has no force. And this follows רבי מאיר, who said: the signing witnesses make the divorce work.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא answers the question by explaining רבי יוחנן's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, the writing of the גט does not need to be לשמה at all, only the signing. So the משנה works even without leaving the תורף blank. That is the opposite of שמואל and עולא, who explained the משנה according to רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: He lets you know, he teaches you
There is no force, no power (here: not needed)
The witnesses who sign the גט

phrases.english: רבי אבא said:
Here he lets you know that 'for her sake' has no force;
phrases.notes: He means there is no need to write the גט for her; only the signing has to be for her.

phrases.english: and it follows רבי מאיר,
who said: the signing witnesses make the divorce work.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: כָּאן הוֹדִיעֲךָ שֶׁאֵין כֹּחַ לִשְׁמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן means that writing לשמה is not needed. The משנה follows רבי מאיר (עדי חתימה כרתי).
steps.whyThisMatters: Now there are two clear ways to explain the משנה: שמואל and עולא follow רבי אלעזר and require the תורף to be left blank, while רבי יוחנן, as explained by רבי אבא, follows רבי מאיר and requires nothing in the writing.

steps.title: But רבה בר בר חנה reported רבי יוחנן differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן that the משנה follows רבי אלעזר, not רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבה בר בר חנה say in the name of רבי יוחנן: it follows רבי אלעזר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction between two reports of what רבי יוחנן said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא just said that, according to רבי יוחנן, the משנה follows רבי מאיר. But רבה בר בר חנה earlier quoted רבי יוחנן saying it follows רבי אלעזר. Both reports cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't (he) say? (introduces a contradiction)

phrases.english: But didn't רבה בר בר חנה say,
in the name of רבי יוחנן:
It follows רבי אלעזר!
phrases.notes: This refers to an earlier statement by רבה בר בר חנה about the same משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אבא's explanation of רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's claim that רבי יוחנן explains the משנה according to רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another report has רבי יוחנן saying the משנה follows רבי אלעזר. The two reports contradict each other.

steps.title: Two אמוראים disagree about רבי יוחנן's view
steps.stepSummary: The answer: these are אמוראים who disagree about what רבי יוחנן held.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are אמוראים, and they disagree about the opinion of רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying the two reporters simply disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no need to make both reports agree. רבי אבא (with רבי זריקא) holds that רבי יוחנן followed רבי מאיר, and רבה בר בר חנה holds that he followed רבי אלעזר. Each is a separate tradition about רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: They are (different) אמוראים, meaning they disagree
According to, about the opinion of

steps.whatToRemember: How to explain the משנה that allows anyone to write a גט: שמואל and עולא (and רבה בר בר חנה's report of רבי יוחנן) follow רבי אלעזר, so the תורף must be left blank. רבי אבא's report of רבי יוחנן follows רבי מאיר, so the writing does not need to be לשמה. The two reports of רבי יוחנן reflect a disagreement between אמוראים.

phrases.english: They are אמוראים
and they disagree about the opinion of רבי יוחנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Disagreement among the people reporting (two traditions of one teacher)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two reports of רבי יוחנן's view cannot both be right, so one explanation must be wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אבא and רבה בר בר חנה are two אמוראים who disagree about what רבי יוחנן held.

steps.title: Who cannot bring a גט
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that anyone may bring a גט except a חרש, a שוטה, a קטן, a סומא, and a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Everyone is fit to bring a bill of divorce, except a deaf-mute, an imbecile, a minor, a blind person, and a gentile.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It names five kinds of people who cannot serve as the messenger who brings a גט to a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The default is that anyone can be the שליח. The משנה then lists five exceptions. The גמרא will later ask why each one is excluded, especially the סומא.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the source text the גמרא is about to discuss)
To bring (deliver) the bill of divorce as a messenger
A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor
A blind person
A non-Jew

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁרִין לְהָבִיא אֶת הַגֵּט,
phrases.english: MISHNAH: All are fit to bring the bill of divorce,
except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor,
and a blind person, and a gentile.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁרִין לְהָבִיא אֶת הַגֵּט, חוּץ מֵחֵרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה. It is not connected to the argument about רבי יוחנן in steps 16 to 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone may be a שליח to bring a גט except a חרש, a שוטה, a קטן, a סומא, or a גוי.

steps.title: Unfit when receiving, fit later: still invalid
steps.stepSummary: If the messenger was unfit when he received the גט and became fit only afterward, he still cannot bring it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a minor received it and then grew up, or a deaf-mute and then could hear, or a blind man and then could see, or an imbecile and then became sane, or a gentile and then converted, he is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה looks at people who were unfit when they were handed the גט but became fit before delivering it. It rules that they are still פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being fit at the moment of delivery is not enough. What went wrong is the start: when he received the גט, he could not legally become a שליח.

keyTerms.meaning: He received (the גט from the husband)
And he grew up (reached adulthood)
And he became sane
And he converted to Judaism
Unfit, invalid

phrases.english: If the minor received it and then grew up; a deaf-mute who then gained his faculties;
a blind man whose eyes then opened; an imbecile who then became sane;
a gentile who then converted: he is unfit.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think that because he is fine by the time he delivers the גט, everything is okay. The משנה says the problem started when he received it.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the list from step 21 to people whose status changed after receiving the גט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A messenger who was unfit when he received the גט stays פסול even if he becomes fit later.

steps.title: Fit, then unfit, then fit again: valid
steps.stepSummary: If the messenger was fit when he received the גט, became unfit for a while, and was fit again by delivery, he is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if someone could hear, then became deaf, then could hear again; or could see, then went blind, then could see again; or was sane, then went insane, then became sane again, he is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite case. The messenger was fit at the start, lost his fitness in the middle, and got it back. Here he is כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Compared with step 22, the difference is that he was fit when he received the גט. A break in the middle does not cancel his appointment as שליח.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with full faculties (can hear and speak)
And he returned (went back to his earlier state)
Sane, mentally competent
Fit, valid

phrases.english: But one who could hear, then became deaf, then again could hear;
one who could see, then became blind, then again could see;
one who was sane, then went insane, then became sane again: he is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 22. Here the messenger was fit at the start.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the messenger was fit at the start and fit again at the end, a period of unfitness in between does not disqualify him.

steps.title: The rule: fit at the start and at the end
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sums up: anyone who has full understanding at the beginning and at the end is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: anyone whose beginning and end are with full understanding is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה wraps up its cases with one general principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters is two moments: when he receives the גט and when he delivers it. If he has proper understanding at both, he is כשר, and the time in between does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
His beginning and his end
With proper understanding (legal competence)

steps.whatToRemember: A שליח for a גט must be fit when he receives it and when he delivers it. Becoming fit only at the end does not help. Losing fitness only in the middle does not hurt.

phrases.aramaic: זֶה הַכְּלָל: כׇּל שֶׁתְּחִילָּתוֹ וְסוֹפוֹ בְּדַעַת – כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: This is the rule: anyone whose beginning and end are with understanding is fit.
phrases.notes: The beginning is when he gets the גט from the husband, and the end is when he hands it to the woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הַכְּלָל: כׇּל שֶׁתְּחִילָּתוֹ וְסוֹפוֹ בְּדַעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the cases in steps 22 and 23 into one general principle.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Fitness is required at the start (receiving) and at the end (delivering). The middle does not matter.

steps.title: Why is a blind person excluded?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why a חרש, a שוטה, a קטן, and a גוי are excluded, but asks why a סומא should be.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It makes sense for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor, since they lack understanding. A gentile also makes sense, since he is not part of the rules that permit remarriage. But a blind person, why not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through the list in the משנה. It accepts the reason for four of the excluded people, and then asks what is wrong with a סומא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חרש, a שוטה, and a קטן lack legal understanding. A גוי is not part of the laws of גיטין. A blind person has full understanding and is Jewish, so the usual reasons do not apply to him. That is why the גמרא asks.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
It makes sense / granted (the case I understand)
People with legal understanding
Someone who is part of the rules that permit (a woman to remarry)
Why?

phrases.english: GEMARA: Granted, a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor,
since they are not people with understanding;

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹי נָמֵי – דְּלָאו בַּר הֶיתֵּירָא הוּא;
phrases.english: a gentile too, since he is not subject to the permitting;
phrases.notes: He means the rules of גט, which free a woman to remarry, do not apply to a non-Jew.

phrases.english: but a blind person, why not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה and questions one item in the list from step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What disqualifies a סומא, who has understanding and is Jewish, from bringing a גט?

steps.title: רב ששת: he cannot see who gave and who received
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that a blind person does not know whom he took the גט from or whom he gave it to.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Because he does not know from whom he takes it and to whom he gives it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question from step 25 by giving the reason a סומא is excluded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not his understanding. It is that he cannot see. He cannot confirm that the husband handed him the גט or that he gave it to the right woman, so he cannot reliably report what happened.

keyTerms.meaning: He takes it
He gives it

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a שליח for a גט needs more than understanding. He must also be able to know who handed him the גט and who received it.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
Because he does not know
from whom he takes it and to whom he gives it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: לְפִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question in step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A סומא cannot identify the person who handed him the גט or the woman he gives it to, so he is unfit.

steps.title: רב יוסף: A blind man can recognize people by their voice
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges רב ששת's reason. If a blind man could not identify people, he would not be allowed to be with his own wife. People are also with their wives in the dark at night. Recognition must work by voice, so the same should work for a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objects: How is a blind man allowed to be with his wife? How are people allowed to be with their wives at night? Rather, they recognize each other by voice. Here too, he can recognize them by voice!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks רב ששת's explanation from Step 26. He argues that a blind man can recognize people by their voice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת claimed a סומא cannot know who handed him the גט. רב יוסף points out that הלכה already trusts voice recognition in marriage, both for a blind man and for anyone in the dark. So voice recognition should also be enough to identify the husband and the wife for a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenges it; raises a strong objection
Recognizing someone by their voice (literally 'an imprint of the eye of the voice')
How?

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objects to it:
phrases.notes: He is objecting to רב ששת's reason from just before: the blind man doesn't know who gave him the גט.

phrases.english: How is a blind man permitted to his wife?

phrases.aramaic: הֵיאַךְ בְּנֵי אָדָם מוּתָּרִים בִּנְשׁוֹתֵיהֶם בַּלַּיְלָה?
phrases.english: How are people permitted to their wives at night?
Rather, it is through recognizing the voice,
here too, it can be through recognizing the voice!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב ששת's answer from Step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's reason that a blind man cannot identify the giver and receiver of the גט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הלכה already relies on voice recognition for a man and his wife, so voice recognition should be enough for a גט too.

steps.title: רב יוסף: The case is a גט from outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives his own reason. The משנה is talking about a גט brought from חוץ לארץ. There the שליח must declare 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם', and a blind man cannot truthfully say that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: Here we are dealing with outside the Land, where he needs to say 'It was written in my presence and signed in my presence,' and he cannot say it.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רב ששת's reason, רב יוסף offers a new reason why a סומא is not fit to bring a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is no longer about identifying people. It is about testimony: a שליח from חוץ לארץ must testify that he saw the גט written and signed. A blind man saw neither, so he cannot give that testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside of ארץ ישראל
We are dealing with
'It was written in my presence and signed in my presence': the declaration a שליח must make for a גט from חוץ לארץ
He is not able

steps.whyThisMatters: It moves the problem from identifying people to the special testimony required for a גט from חוץ לארץ.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said:
Here we are dealing with outside the Land;
where he needs to say:
'It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence,'
phrases.notes: This is the declaration a שליח must make when he brings a גט from outside ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: and he cannot say it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reason rejected in Step 27 with a new one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A סומא was thought to be unfit because he cannot identify people.
steps.terutzMaskana: A סומא is unfit because, for a גט from חוץ לארץ, he cannot testify that he saw it written and signed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A סומא cannot bring a גט from חוץ לארץ, because he cannot declare 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם'.

steps.title: אביי: Then someone who saw and later went blind should be fit
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף. Suppose a person could see when the גט was written and signed, and only later went blind. He can still say 'בפני נכתב', so by רב יוסף's reason he should be fit. But the משנה implies he is fit only if he regains his sight.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, someone who could see and then became blind, who can say it, should also be fit?! But it is taught: one who could see, became blind, and could see again is fit. If he could see again, yes; if he could not see again, no!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tests רב יוסף's reason against the wording of the משנה. He tries to show that the reason does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רב יוסף's reason, what matters is having seen the writing and signing. A man who saw them before going blind should therefore be fit even if he stays blind. Yet the משנה lists the case of one who 'could see again', which implies that a man who stays blind is unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: But now, if so: introduces a challenge from what the last view implies
Could see, then became blind
And then could see again
But it is taught: brings a source to challenge
Yes

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But if so, one who could see and then became blind,
who is able to say it, would he also be fit?!
phrases.notes: He saw the גט written and signed before he went blind, so he can make the declaration.

phrases.english: But it is taught:
one who could see, became blind, and again could see, is fit –
if he again could see, yes;
if he did not again see, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's reason from Step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's reason that the problem is only the inability to say 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By רב יוסף's reason, a man who went blind after seeing should be fit. But the משנה's wording implies he is fit only if he regains his sight.

steps.title: The משנה mentions regaining sight only to match the שוטה case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a man who stays blind is fit too. The משנה wrote 'could see again' only to match its parallel case of a שוטה. There, regaining sanity really is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same law applies even if he did not see again. But since it teaches 'sane, became a שוטה, and became sane again', where the reason is that he became sane again and otherwise not, it also taught 'could see, became blind, and could see again.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יוסף. It explains that the משנה's wording about regaining sight is only there for style, not because it changes the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a שוטה, regaining sanity matters, because he must understand what he is doing at the time of delivery. The משנה wrote the blind case in the same pattern to keep the two cases parallel. So no inference can be drawn from it, and רב יוסף's reason stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The same law applies
Since it teaches: the wording is copied to match a nearby case
Was sane, then became a שוטה
The reason is

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יוסף, a סומא cannot bring a גט from חוץ לארץ because he cannot testify that he saw it written and signed. Someone who saw and only later went blind is fit. The משנה's 'could see again' just copies the שוטה pattern.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't learn from the משנה's wording that regaining sight is required. The גמרא says it is only there to match the שוטה case, where regaining sanity really is required.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא הַדִּין דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא חָזַר וְנִתְפַּתֵּחַ;
phrases.english: The same is true even if he did not again become able to see;
but since it teaches
phrases.notes: The משנה wrote the blind case to match the case right next to it, not to teach something new.

phrases.english: one who was sane, became insane, and became sane again –
where the reason he is fit is that he became sane again,
but if he did not become sane again – not;

phrases.aramaic: תְּנָא נָמֵי פָּתוּחַ וְנִסְתַּמֵּא וְחָזַר וְנִתְפַּתֵּחַ.
phrases.english: it also taught: one who could see, became blind, and again could see.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא הַדִּין דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא חָזַר וְנִתְפַּתֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from Step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic wording (איידי): the phrase only copies a parallel case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's wording implies that a man who stays blind is unfit.
steps.terutzMaskana: A man who saw and then went blind is fit. The משנה's wording only mirrors the שוטה case.

steps.title: The wording of the rule supports the answer
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי proves from the משנה's general rule that only sound mind (דעת) is required at the beginning and the end, not full fitness. So a man who stays blind is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The wording of the משנה also shows this. It says, 'This is the rule: anyone who has sound mind at the beginning and at the end is fit.' It does not say, 'anyone who is fit at the beginning and at the end is fit.' Learn from this that the answer is correct.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings support from the exact wording of the משנה for the answer just given in step 30, that a man who stays blind is also fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule says 'בדעת', meaning a clear mind. It does not say 'בכשרות', meaning fully fit in every way. A blind man has a clear mind both when he receives the גט and when he delivers it, so he passes the rule even though he never sees again.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording also proves it; the exact words of the משנה support this point
This is the general rule
With sound mind, mentally clear and aware
In full fitness, qualified in every way
Learn from it; the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's test is clear mind (דעת) at the start and at the end. A man who goes blind after seeing the גט written and signed, and stays blind, is still fit to bring it.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two words. 'בדעת' is about the mind, so a שוטה fails it. 'בכשרות' would mean fully fit, and a blind man might fail that. The משנה chose 'בדעת'.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The wording is also precise, for it teaches:
This is the general rule:
anyone who has sound mind at the beginning and at the end is fit;
phrases.notes: 'Beginning' is when he receives the גט from the husband, and 'end' is when he hands it to the woman.

phrases.english: and it does not teach:
anyone who is fit at the beginning and at the end is fit;
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings textual support for the answer in step 30 that a man who stays blind is fit.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a man who becomes blind after the writing and signing, and stays blind, is fit as a שליח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's general rule uses the word 'בדעת' (sound mind) and not 'בכשרות' (full fitness).

steps.title: Can a slave be an agent to receive a divorce document?
steps.stepSummary: A new question is put to רבי אמי: may an עבד be appointed as a שליח to receive a woman's גט from her husband?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רבי אמי: What is the law for a slave? Can he be made an agent to receive a woman's גט from her husband?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. Scholars ask רבי אמי whether an עבד can be a שליח who receives a גט for a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the שליח is not bringing the גט to the woman. He receives it for her, so that once it reaches his hand she is divorced. The question is whether an עבד counts as a valid שליח for this job.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked him; a real question put to a scholar
A Canaanite slave
What is the law?
To receive a גט on the woman's behalf

phrases.english: They asked Rabbi Ami:
A slave, what is the law,
can he be made an agent
to receive a woman's divorce document
phrases.notes: This kind of שליח is appointed by the wife and receives the גט for her. He is not just bringing it to her.

phrases.english: from the hand of her husband?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of the blind שליח ends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an עבד is a valid שליח to receive a גט for a woman from her husband.

steps.title: רבי אמי starts from the gentile's disqualification
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי begins his answer by pointing out that the משנה disqualifies a גוי. His full answer continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: From the fact that the משנה disqualifies a גוי...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי starts to answer. He points to the משנה, which lists a גוי among the people who cannot bring a גט. The rest of his answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי does not give a direct yes or no. He builds his answer on what the משנה included and left out of its list of people who are disqualified. This line only sets up his reasoning, which is finished in the next section.

keyTerms.meaning: Disqualifies
A non-Jew, whom the משנה disqualifies from bringing a גט

phrases.english: He said to them:
From the fact that it disqualifies a gentile,
phrases.notes: 'It' is our משנה, which lists a גוי among those who cannot bring a גט.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר להו מדקא פסיל ליה לגוי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins רבי אמי's answer to the question about an עבד.
